description: Composite six-panel Thermo-Calc® (CALPHAD) figure for the Fe-11.15Mn-5.6Al-0.07C system. (a) plots "Mass percent of Mn in all phases" (0-100) against "Temperature [°C]" (0-1600) with legend MN in BCC_A2 (blue), MN in FCC_A1 (red), MN in FCC_A1#2 (green): red Mn-in-FCC_A1 falls from ~74 mass% at 0 °C to ~14 mass% near 900 °C, blue Mn-in-BCC_A2 rises from ~1 to ~12 mass%, green MN in FCC_A1#2 stays near 95-96 mass%. (b) does the same for Al (0-7 mass%): AL in BCC_A2 stays ~6.2 falling to ~5.5 mass%, AL in FCC_A1 rises from ~1.5 to ~5 mass% near 700-900 °C then declines, AL in FCC_A1#2 is ~0. Both (a) and (b) carry a vertical black line at ~950 °C labelled "Experimented Temperature" with green and red markers. (c,e) plot Gibbs Free Energy (J/mol, -38500/-42000 and -42000/-46000) versus %Mn (6-20) at 500 and 550 °C; (d,f) versus %Al (2-10) at 500 and 550 °C, BCC black and FCC red. In each, point A marks the BCC/FCC intersection (equal Gibbs energy), C the BCC composition and B the FCC composition, with green/red arrows delimiting BCC- and FCC-dominant regions and a "Experimented Nominal Composition" vertical line.

subfigures.description: Line plot of mass percent of Mn in all phases (0-100) versus Temperature [°C] (0-1600). Legend: MN in BCC_A2 (blue, rising ~1→12 mass%), MN in FCC_A1 (red, falling ~74→14 mass%), MN in FCC_A1#2 (green, flat ~95-96 mass%). A vertical line at ~950 °C labelled 'Experimented Temperature' carries a green and a red marker.

Line plot of mass percent of Al in all phases (0-7) versus Temperature [°C] (0-1600). Legend: AL in BCC_A2 (blue, ~6.2→5.5 mass%), AL in FCC_A1 (red, rising ~1.5→~5 mass% then falling), AL in FCC_A1#2 (green, ~0). Same 'Experimented Temperature' vertical line at ~950 °C with green and red markers.

Gibbs Free Energy (J/mol, -38500 to -42000) versus %Mn (6-20) at 500 °C. Black BCC and red FCC curves intersect near 14.5 %Mn; point A sits at the intersection (~-40900 J/mol), C (green) on BCC at ~10.5 %Mn, B (red) on FCC at ~13 %Mn. Green arrow = BCC Dominant Region, red arrow = FCC Dominant Region; vertical line 'Experimented Nominal Composition' at ~11 %Mn; dashed horizontal and vertical guides through A.

Gibbs Free Energy (J/mol, -30000 to -50000) versus %Al (2-10) at 500 °C. BCC (black) and FCC (red) curves nearly coincide, BCC lying slightly lower; label 'A~0.8% Al' near the upper left of the curves; B (red) at ~4.7 %Al and C (green) at ~5.8 %Al; a green arrow marks BCC Dominant Region across 2-10 %Al and a vertical line marks the Experimented Nominal Composition.

Gibbs Free Energy (J/mol, -42000 to -46000) versus %Mn (6-20) at 550 °C. BCC and FCC curves cross at point A near 13.5 %Mn; C (green) on BCC at ~10.5 %Mn and B (red) just left of A. Green BCC Dominant Region arrow and red FCC Dominant Region arrow plus the 'Experimented Nominal Composition' vertical line.

Gibbs Free Energy (J/mol, -36000 to -50000) versus %Al (2-10) at 550 °C. Curves cross near ~5.7 %Al; A (top, dashed vertical to x-axis) at ~2.9 %Al, B (red) at ~4.8 %Al, C (green) at ~6 %Al. A short red arrow marks an FCC Dominant Region only to ~2.9 %Al, with a green BCC Dominant Region arrow over the remainder.

observations.observation: Panel (a) axes are labelled 'Mass percent of Mn in all phases' (0-100) and 'Temperature [°C]' (0-1600); the legend entries are 'MN in BCC_A2' (blue), 'MN in FCC_A1' (red) and 'MN in FCC_A1#2' (green).

In (a) the Mn content of FCC_A1 decreases monotonically from about 74 mass% at 0 °C to about 14 mass% near 900 °C, while Mn in BCC_A2 increases from about 1 mass% to about 12 mass% and Mn in FCC_A1#2 remains nearly flat at about 95-96 mass%.
Both (a) and (b) contain a vertical black line at roughly 950 °C labelled 'Experimented Temperature', marked with a green point (higher value) and a red point (lower value).

In (b) Al in BCC_A2 stays high, about 6.2 mass% at 0 °C falling to about 5.5 mass% at 1200 °C, whereas Al in FCC_A1 rises from about 1.5 mass% at 0 °C to a maximum of about 5 mass% near 700-900 °C and then decreases; Al in FCC_A1#2 is essentially zero.

In (c) (500 °C, Gibbs Free Energy in J/mol from -38500 to -42000 versus %Mn from 6 to 20) the black BCC and red FCC curves intersect at point A near 14.5 %Mn at approximately -40900 J/mol, and the green arrow marks BCC Dominant Region up to that intersection with the red arrow marking FCC Dominant Region beyond it.
In (c) a vertical line labelled 'Experimented Nominal Composition' lies at about 11 %Mn, with point C (green) on the BCC curve near 10.5 %Mn and point B (red) on the FCC curve near 13 %Mn.

In (d) (500 °C versus %Al, 2-10) the BCC curve lies equal to or slightly below the FCC curve over the whole composition range, a single green arrow labels the BCC Dominant Region across 2-10 %Al, and the annotation 'A~0.8% Al' is printed near the top of the curves; B (red) is at about 4.7 %Al and C (green) at about 5.8 %Al.
Comparing (c) with (e), raising the isothermal section from 500 to 550 °C shifts the BCC/FCC intersection point A to a lower Mn content, from about 14.5 %Mn in (c) to about 13.5 %Mn in (e).

In (f) (550 °C versus %Al) an FCC Dominant Region exists only below about 2.9 %Al, marked by a short red arrow, while the BCC Dominant Region covers the rest of the 2-10 %Al axis; point A lies at the top of the curves at about 2.9 %Al, B at about 4.8 %Al and C at about 6 %Al.
The caption states the Thermo-Calc calculations are for the equilibrium condition of the experimented Fe-11.15Mn-5.6Al-0.07C system.

The caption defines point A as the point where the Gibbs Free Energy of FCC and BCC is equal thermodynamically, and points B and C as the FCC and BCC chemical compositions resulting from elemental partitioning, extracted from (a, b) and Table 1.
The citing text states that Thermo-Calc predicts BCC_A2 (ferrite), FCC_A1 (austenite) and BCC_A1#2, the latter a BCC-structured phase containing an extremely high amount of Mn.

The citing text states that Mn is partitioned more into austenite and Al more into ferrite, and that an EDS elemental map of the microstructure deformed at 500 °C shows almost similar partitioning (compare Table 1 and Fig. 4a-b).

The citing text asserts that applying the nominal composition gives different Gibbs free energies for ferrite and austenite at 500 °C in Fig. 4c, but that using the elemental partitioning of Fig. 4a-b and Table 1 gives the same Gibbs free energy for both phases (the dashed line in Fig. 4c).

measured_quantities: mass percent of Mn in each phase (mass%)
mass percent of Al in each phase (mass%)
unreadable_items: Exact numerical values of the green and red markers on the 'Experimented Temperature' line in (a) and (b) are not printed on the figure; only curve positions relative to the axes can be read.
Exact coordinates of point A in (c), (e) and (f) are not printed as numbers; they must be read from the crossing of the curves and the dashed guide lines.
